kill_argument: The only 'holds' for H1 and the only 'holds' for H2a both come from electricity, a half-hourly time series split at random. The check the design assigned to that leak, sens-elec-time, cannot answer the question. Under the chronological split every model's uncalibrated ECE is 0.17-0.33 (0.02-0.05 under random splits). Recalibrating on the calibration quarter makes LR worse (Brier 0.202 to 0.253), and HGB's Brier starts at 0.327. So its 'H2a contradicted' and 'H2b holds (-0.078)' measure drift from the calibration quarter to the test quarter, confounded with the fill regime and with date extrapolation. They do not measure leakage. The absolute levels that show this were computed but left out of claims.jsonl. The overall verdicts do not hinge on electricity (H1 is contradicted on bank-marketing and phoneme; H2a is inconclusive either way), so the remedy is narrowing, not rejection. What I attacked that held: all 16 categories and 4 overall verdicts recomputed from cells.csv; all five analysis scripts re-executed in scratch, every output byte-identical; ledger order (F1 fix and plan narrowing before main); H1 against the estimator floor (floor-adjusted intervals still contradicted); precedence for H2b; ece_db never used as a licence.

findings.text: Carried from code-r1 F3 (isotonic on the logit is not isotonic on the probability between calibration points). design.method step 7 now says the two are equal only at the calibration points and that scikit-learn interpolates linearly in the logit between them, and that the paper describes the calibrator that way. No code changed.

Sensitivity (c) cannot do what analysis_plan[8] says it does ('show whether random-split temporal leakage drives the electricity results'). The claims report its categories without the numbers that show why. Electricity supplies the only H1 'holds' (+0.0270) and the only H2a 'holds' (-0.0028). Under the chronological split, every uncalibrated model is badly miscalibrated: ECE 0.168 (LR), 0.169 (RF), 0.334 (HGB), against 0.022, 0.049 and 0.028 under random splits. AUC drops to 0.83-0.84 from 0.94 for RF and HGB. Recalibration fitted on the calibration quarter makes LR worse on the test quarter (Brier 0.202 none, 0.251 Platt, 0.253 isotonic; ECE 0.168 to 0.262), so the calibration and test quarters differ in distribution. Three things change at once. (i) The Victoria fill rows sit only in train (7,642-7,753; calibration and test have 0), which threats[4] discloses. (ii) The normalised date column is a feature, and the test quarter's dates lie beyond most of the training range. (iii) The calibration quarter and the test quarter differ. 'H2a contradicted' (+0.0265 [+0.0209, +0.0322]) and 'H2b holds' (-0.0782 [-0.1013, -0.0551]) therefore measure whether isotonic fitted on the calibration quarter happens to move a badly shifted model toward the test quarter. They do not measure whether random-split leakage inflates main's electricity results. The per-model chronological levels are in runs/sens-elec-time/metrics.json (electricity_time_<model>_<cal>_<metric>_mean) but none is in claims.jsonl, so the Writer cannot state them with a macro, and a reader of the claims sees only the categories. The cheapest remedy is to narrow, with no new run. (a) Add claims for the chronological none and isotonic ECE, Brier and AUC per model, and for LR's Brier rise under recalibration. (b) Reword the r-h*_time-electricity-* claims and NOTES: under the chronological split all three models are miscalibrated by 0.17-0.33 ECE, the calibration and test quarters are shifted, and the run therefore cannot tell whether main's electricity 'holds' come from random-split leakage. (c) The paper says plainly that the leakage question for electricity is open. The overall verdicts do not depend on it: H1 stays contradicted and H2a stays inconclusive if electricity is dropped.

findings.text: sens-ncal reports an overall k-of-4 verdict for H2a ('contradicted') and H2b ('inconclusive') as claims r-h2a-ncal-overall and r-h2b-ncal-overall. The plan asks only that 'H2a and H2b categories [be] recomputed' (analysis_plan[7], design.method step 12(b)), not for an overall verdict. That verdict mixes three refits on 1,351 calibration rows with phoneme's main cells. The H2a 'contradicted' rests on mean increases of +0.00087 (adult) and +0.00084 (bank-marketing), whose intervals [+0.00054, +0.00121] and [+0.00056, +0.00112] cross the 0.001 margin only at their upper end. Each claim is labelled verdict-neutral, but an overall 'contradicted' is the most quotable sensitivity number and is a post hoc aggregation. Remedy: drop the two overall claims, or relabel them as an aggregation not in the plan, and report the per-dataset categories with their intervals.

findings.text: Two readings that the claims allow but the evidence does not support. (a) H1 'contradicted' comes from LR's own miscalibration, not from RF being well calibrated. On bank-marketing LR none has ECE 0.031 (ece_db 0.030). On phoneme it has ECE 0.063 (ece_db 0.055), Platt leaves it at 0.063, and LR's AUC is 0.81 against RF's 0.95: a linear model that is misspecified on a nonlinear problem. RF none still has ECE 0.016 and 0.037 there, and isotonic lowers RF's ECE on all four datasets. My floor check (below) confirms that the contradiction is not a floor artefact, but what it shows is 'default LR was worse calibrated than default RF on these two datasets'. It does not show 'RF is well calibrated'. (b) H2b 'no difference' covers intervals that lie wholly on both sides of zero. On adult, [+0.00008, +0.00042] means isotonic raised HGB Brier on 9 of 10 seeds. On bank-marketing and electricity the intervals lie wholly below zero. All are inside +/-0.001. Under the pre-registered precedence the category is correct, but it means 'a change smaller than 0.001 Brier', not 'no effect'. Remedy: wording in the r-h1-overall and r-h2b-overall claim texts and in the paper. No new run.
